issues.description: Inconsistent bytes-per-pixel (pixel stride) between the problem statement/template expectation and the solution implementation. The problem statement explicitly says 24-bit color is rounded to 32 bits (i.e. 4 bytes per pixel) (problem_statement.md lines 17-19). In the solution, the set_pixel routine multiplies x by 3 (mov edx, 3; mul edx) to compute the x offset (solution_repository/pixel.asm lines 19-34), while elsewhere in the solution the code uses a 4-byte stride for x (mov edi, 4; mul edi and stride 7680 = 1920*4 in solution_repository/pixel.asm lines 94-100). This mismatch (3 vs 4 bytes per pixel) will compute incorrect addresses and cause incorrect memory writes, and it directly contradicts the problem description that pixels are stored as 4 bytes. Students will be confused which stride to implement and may produce code that writes at wrong addresses or corrupts memory.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the bytes-per-pixel (pixel stride) consistent and match the problem statement (4 bytes per pixel). Concretely: change the set_pixel implementation to compute offset = x*4 + y*(1920*4) + display_start (e.g., multiply x by 4 or shift left by 2 instead of multiplying by 3). Ensure all address calculations (both in set_pixel and in main) use the same stride constant (7680) and write the 4-byte pixel value at that computed address.
